title: Mental Health Crisis, Panic & Suicidal Thoughts
summary: Stay calm and with the person, listen without judging, keep them safe, and connect them with help – a crisis line or emergency services.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} if anyone is in immediate danger
when: They have harmed themselves or have a plan and the means to do so now
They are a danger to others
They may have taken an overdose – see Opioid overdose / Poisoning
Otherwise, call or text {CRISIS} for support

steps.title: Make it safe
steps.text: Check for dangers to them, you and others. If safe, remove means of harm. Do not put yourself at risk.

steps.title: Stay with them and stay calm
steps.text: Speak slowly and simply. Introduce yourself. Listen without judging or arguing.

steps.title: Ask directly about suicide
steps.text: If you are worried, ask: "Are you thinking about killing yourself?" Asking does not put the idea in their head.

steps.title: Panic attack
steps.text: Help them sit somewhere quieter. Encourage slow breathing – in through the nose, out slowly through the mouth – and reassure them it will pass.
steps.caution: Chest pain, breathlessness or fainting may be a medical emergency – do not assume it is panic.

steps.title: Connect them with help
steps.text: Call or text {CRISIS}, or call {EMERGENCY} if they are in immediate danger. Offer to make the call with them.

steps.title: Do not leave them alone
steps.text: Stay with them until help arrives or they are with someone they trust.

warningSigns: Talking about wanting to die or having a plan
doNot: Do not leave someone at risk alone
Do not promise to keep a suicide plan secret
Do not argue, threaten or make them feel guilty
Do not put yourself in danger
